hints: Focus on the two C=C bonds in compound X, each one will use up one molecule of HBr in an electrophilic addition.
Recall Markovnikov's rule, the H adds to the carbon that already has more H atoms so the Br ends up on the more substituted, more stable carbocation carbon.
Apply that rule separately to the trisubstituted double bond on the left and the terminal double bond on the right to place both Br atoms.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two alkenes in X**

Look closely at the skeleton. Compound X is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$.

There is a trisubstituted C=C on the left (C2=C3) and a terminal monosubstituted C=C on the right (C6=C7). Each needs one $\text{HBr}$:
$$\text{C}=\text{C} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}-\text{CBr}$$

**Add HBr to the left-hand double bond**

The left bond is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$. C2 has one H, C3 has no H.

H adds to C2 (the carbon with more H), and a tertiary carbocation forms at C3. Br then attaches to C3 to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)-$. This is Markovnikov addition.

**Add HBr to the right-hand double bond**

The right bond is $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. C7 is $\text{CH}_2$ with two H, C6 is $\text{CH}$ with one H.

H adds to the terminal C7, and a secondary carbocation forms at C6. Br then attaches to C6 to give $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_3$. Again this is Markovnikov addition.

**Combine to get the major product**

Putting both additions together gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{Br})(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Br})\text{CH}_3$.

That is a tertiary bromide at position 3 and a secondary bromide at position 6, which matches the major product.

options.A: Correct. Br is on the tertiary carbon on the left (C3) and on the secondary internal carbon on the right (C6). Both positions follow Markovnikov addition via the most stable carbocations.
options.B: Incorrect. The left Br is correctly placed on the tertiary carbon, but the right Br is on the terminal primary carbon. That would require H to add to the internal carbon to give an unstable primary carbocation, which is anti-Markovnikov and not favoured.
options.C: Incorrect. The right Br is correctly placed, but the left Br is on the secondary carbon C2. That would come from a secondary carbocation at C2 instead of the much more stable tertiary carbocation at C3, so it is the minor product for that double bond.
options.D: Incorrect. Both Br atoms are in anti-Markovnikov positions, on C2 on the left and on the terminal C7 on the right. This ignores carbocation stability completely and would give the least stable intermediates.
